name: Northwest Territories
summary_text: Direction on record: worse than national on gendered lethal violence, better/neutral on official climate. No trans-specific territorial legislation, incident series or policing pattern was found for the Northwest Territories; national criminal law, the national self-declaration gender framework and national protections apply directly. The territory-level figure on record is gendered lethal violence: in 2021 the three territories recorded 3.20 gender-related homicides per 100,000 women and girls, roughly triple the highest provincial rate (1.03), with rural areas more than 2.5x urban rates — not trans-specific, but the only official territorial rate data available. Nationally, police-reported gender-identity/expression-motivated hate crimes rose 8% to 139 in 2024 — a fourth consecutive annual increase, nearly triple the 2020 level — and Pride-season June runs roughly double the monthly average for sexual-orientation-motivated incidents.

sources.title: The Daily — Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024
sources.claim_summary: Statistics Canada release 'Police-reported hate crime in Canada, 2024' (published 30 March 2026): 4,882 police-reported hate crimes (+1%; +169% since 2018; rate 11.9 per 100,000). Gender identity/expression-motivated incidents rose 8% to 139, a fourth consecutive increase (+184% since 2020); sexual-orientation-motivated incidents fell 26% to 658, with June 2024 (113) more than double the ~50-incident monthly average. Rates are ~2.5x higher in metropolitan areas than smaller towns — thin metropolitan reporting infrastructure applies to the territories.
